routes.name: Cascadian Route
routes.approach: Multi-stage approach (~11+ miles): drive to Chelan, ferry to Lucerne, bus to Holden Village, then hike to a camp at about 7,000 ft near the North Star-Bonanza col - a full day of travel and approach.
routes.descent: From the Southwest Summit, downclimb/traverse to the Isella Glacier and descend along an undulating line of steep rock and moraine at about two-thirds of the glacier's height, then cross through a notch in the south ridge to regain the North Star-Bon

routes.name: Oregonian Route
routes.approach: Standard approach follows the same Lucerne ferry -> Holden Village -> hike to the North Star-Bonanza col camp used for the Soviet Route; the first-ascent party's much longer bike-and-hike approach was due to temporary ferry/road closures in 2013 and is not typical.

routes.name: Brothers Traverse (North Peak to South Peak)
routes.approach: Follow the same Lena Lake / Brothers Trail approach used for the South Couloir to established climbers' camp (~6 miles from the trailhead), then cross the creek westward, cross a slide meadow and old burn scar, and climb a wide gully north to about 5,500 ft to gain the North Peak side of the mountain.

routes.name: Central Mowich Face
routes.description: Central Mowich Face offers two route variations on the northwest face of Mount Rainier. Route follows steep snow and ice sections on a north-facing glacier. Two main variations exist: Grade III (direct, snow-dominant) and Grade IV (ice-steep variation).
routes.approach: Mowich Lake has had no road access since the SR 165 Fairfax Bridge closed in April 2025, with no detour; reaching the lake now means a long walk in on the Wonderland Trail from another part of the park. From Mowich Lake, take the Wonderland Trail 4 miles to Spray Park. Climbers trail ascends lower Ptarmigan Ridge. At 8,300 ft, descend 1,000 ft to North Mowich Glacier.
routes.descent: From Liberty Cap or the main summit, descend via Emmons-Winthrop to Camp Schurman, or via Disappointment Cleaver to Camp Muir, depending on party preference and conditions.

routes.name: North Mowich Headwall
routes.description: North Mowich Headwall (Edmunds Headwall) is a steep Grade IV ice and mixed route on the north side of Mount Rainier. Features sustained steep slopes and narrow hourglass rock/ice section.
routes.approach: Northwest corner of Mount Rainier National Park, from Mowich Lake; the SR 165 road to the lake has had no public access since the Fairfax Bridge closed permanently in April 2025
routes.descent: From Liberty Cap, cross to the main summit area or descend directly via Emmons-Winthrop to Camp Schurman.

routes.name: Tahoma Cleaver
routes.approach: From Westside Road — Dry Creek Trailhead, walk the closed road past the barricade to the Tahoma Creek Trail and climb it about 2 miles to the Wonderland Trail junction near 4300 ft. Go south over the Tahoma Creek suspension bridge, follow the Wonderland Trail to Indian Henry's Hunting Ground, then take the Mirror Lakes Trail until it fades in the basin between Copper and Pyramid Peaks. routes.name: East Route
routes.approach: From the Stuart Lake trailhead, take the Colchuck Lake branch roughly 4 miles and about 2,300 feet up to the lake. Follow the shore to its far end, then rock-hop up the glacier moraine and the steep slope above it to the top of Aasgard Pass, where this route begins.

routes.name: Triple Couloirs
routes.approach: Stuart Lake Trailhead to Colchuck Lake (4.5 mi, ~2,000 ft gain), then approach the base of the north face aiming for the lowest rock protrusion near the middle of the wall to find the Hidden Couloir entrance around 6,400 ft.

routes.name: West Route
routes.approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead, follow the Stuart Lake trail about 2.5 miles to the split, then bear left on the Colchuck Lake trail for roughly 1.6 miles to Colchuck Lake. Continue up the Colchuck Glacier to Colchuck Col, where the route begins; a snow gully on the peak's south side leads from there to the summit ridge.

routes.name: This, My Friend
routes.approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (3,400 ft) follow Stuart Lake Trail #1599 to the signed junction with Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A at 2.6 miles, then continue to Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft) at roughly 4.3-4.4 miles and about 2,200 ft of gain. routes.name: South Face
routes.approach: From Highway 97 south of the Y-junction, drive ~7.5 miles and turn onto Ingalls Creek Road/Trailhead. Hike the Ingalls Creek Trail roughly 8 miles, then leave the trail (right/north) into brushy terrain up Crystal Creek, gaining about 2,200 ft to a base-camp meadow and tarn near 6,000 ft. routes.descent: From the summit plateau, descend north/northeast down talus and slab slopes toward Crystal Lake, then pick up the outlet stream drainage and follow it back down to the Crystal Creek base-camp meadow/tarn, retracing the approach back to Ingalls Creek
